title: A Deterministic Chain-of-Custody Graph for an AI Governance Corpus: Bitcoin Hash-Anchoring, Self-Healing Re-Anchoring, and Fail-Closed Reconciliation — With Two Live Drift Catches and a Disclosed Self-Correction (SIP-034..037)
description:
SQUIRL OS RESEARCH DISCLOSURE — READ FIRST: AI-assisted, receipt-first research program (open-book doctrine: audit-and-correction, versioned amendments, append-only public ledger). Errors are disclosed, not erased. This software is a prototype and is provided for educational and research purposes only. Not intended for production use, commercial deployment, or safety-critical environments. All payloads synthetic. No customer-identifiable data appears in this record (POL-DISC-001).

A deterministic chain-of-custody graph binding an AI governance corpus to the Bitcoin blockchain — with self-healing re-anchoring and fail-closed reconciliation. While the 'everything on chain' wave puts data and logic on-chain, this record documents the opposite design: an append-only AI governance corpus (ledger, monitoring feed, preregistrations, receipts) whose integrity is anchored by Bitcoin proof-of-work via OpenTimestamps — only 32-byte SHA-256 digests cross the boundary; no tokens, wallets, or non-digest data touch any chain, and cryptographic authority remains in a separate post-quantum layer (CRYSTALS-Dilithium3, kyber_1024, SPHINCS+-256f; the existence/authority split is disclosed by design).

The novel contribution is the closed loop. Three deterministic services (no LLM in any decision path): STAMP (hash-only anchoring, dual-calendar redundancy), RECOVER (drift detection with automatic re-anchoring that retires superseded stamps to history as retained proof — never deleted), and RECONCILE (a fail-closed gate classifying every receipt as LIVE MATCH / CERTIFIED STATE / ORPHAN). Benchmarking the gate against its own live ledger caught two genuine drift events on its first two runs, the second revealing a structural property we formalize as the tip-lag corollary (INV-1-C): an append-only log's tip is always ahead of its most recent stamp — mirroring Bitcoin checkpoint semantics — solved with certified state snapshots so every receipt reconciles deterministically.

Disclosed self-correction (audit-and-correction doctrine): a benchmark-PASS claim was sealed in ledger entry 0165 before the gate returned; the gate returned FAIL. Entry 0166 corrects the record — premature claim disclosed, root cause structural, fix disclosed, nothing scrubbed — and the correction is itself an entry in the anchored ledger. Final verdict: PASS — 3/3 live and certified receipts matched, 1 historical retained, 0 orphans.

Scoped novelty claim: hash-anchoring itself is established prior art (OpenTimestamps, RFC 3161, Chainpoint, Proof of Existence — cited, not claimed). To our knowledge, this is the first reported end-to-end automated chain-of-custody system for an AI governance corpus integrating hash-only PoW anchoring, deterministic drift re-anchoring with historical retention, fail-closed reconciliation gating, and a disclosed self-correction of its own benchmark record. Independent verification trusts no party: pip install opentimestamps-client; ots upgrade; ots verify.

Scope caveat (load-bearing): anchoring proves existence, not authority; Bitcoin's signatures are not post-quantum (hence INV-4). Prototype software; all payloads synthetic. Dual Mesh Benchmark status: NOT MEASURED in this record (no neural-mesh inference involved); program benchmark DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23321637 (DeepSeek column 10.5281/zenodo.23345241). Provenance: append-only public ledger entries 0162-0166, github.com/LLong2026/four-horsemen. DCAI community: zenodo.org/communities/dcai.
